records.rationale: Full three-path patch read. Retain emulated metadata-page subtraction, sysctl_perf_event_mlock linkage/header declaration and initcall default 512+reported-page KiB. Positive local simpleperf uses (mmap_pages+1)*sysconf(_SC_PAGE_SIZE) and the kernel data_offset/data_size; SDK goldfish page_shift=14 selects 16 KiB. cef6ed5fe6a4 adds an explicit minimum-size guard before unsigned subtraction and balances unaccounting for all physical metadata pages. Native mmap bounds, power-of-two data requirement, resource/capability checks, event revocation, PMU callbacks and failed-map cleanup remain. Kernel default becomes 528 KiB in 16 KiB mode, but local init-perfetto.rc can later set 516 KiB; no claim of the eventual runtime setting. This candidate does not resolve the separate filemap shared-EOF issue.

records.rationale: Full three-path patch read. Retain zeroed higher-order metadata allocation/free, reported data_offset, vmalloc sizing/data offset and metadata/data translation for 4/8/16 KiB. Adapt cef6ed5fe6a4: cast user_page to char* before byte arithmetic; otherwise the 1088-byte struct type scales pgoff*4096 into a multi-megabyte displacement outside a 16 KiB metadata allocation, potentially exposing unrelated memory or crashing. Also make the full allocated metadata area writable while data/AUX remain read-only, require AUX to start beyond all metadata and data, and retain LTS PFN lifetime rules by removing obsolete page->mapping clearing. The last change preserves native current struct-page restrictions rather than ACK obsolete cleanup. Allocate/free orders match the boot-only immutable reported page size. Whole regular allocator cleanup is native apart from metadata helpers; full map_range/perf_mmap/lifetime functions equal LTS. No real perf mapping or exploit was executed.

validation: Host extracted-code check passed 15,076 cases. Old control produced 32 wrong metadata addresses, 32 write-permission mismatches, 2,430 unbalanced unaccounts and 32 accepted AUX overlaps. No malformed-size mismatch was reproduced; minimum-size check is explicit defensive validation. Initial harness compilation omitted the multiline mapping return type; fixed the harness, not kernel code, and then ran both controls. Build 148 passed, producing the kernel image, 100 common modules and 45 virtual-device modules. All 145 signatures and module flag/CRC tables verified; modified-payload negative control rejected. runtime perf mappings, allocator failure, locking/concurrent teardown and page-table behavior are unverified.
security: All expanded writable pages are inside the zeroed metadata allocation, not data/AUX pages. This intentionally adapts the native one-physical-page permission boundary to one reported userspace metadata page. Old accounting retained extra charges after unmap, causing overcharging/resource denial; no accounting bypass exploit is claimed. AUX overlap can select auxiliary pages within the logical normal buffer boundary; runtime impact unverified. Keep native VM_PFNMAP, refcounts, locks and invalidation/cleanup rather than reintroduce page->mapping writes or VM_MIXEDMAP behavior.

stable_fix_review.assessment: Full three-path stable fix read. Native perf_mmap and perf_mmap_close bodies remain exact, including minimal first-exposure cleanup under mmap_mutex and complex close outside that mutex. Native ring_buffer_init and entire internal.h preserve mmap_user lifetime/refcount initialization and RCU free_uid. The only overlap is perf_mmap_unaccount arithmetic: replace one physical metadata page with __PAGE_SIZE/PAGE_SIZE, retaining both atomic decrements and the same helper/call placement. This corrects enlarged-metadata overcharging without reintroducing the mutex recursion or failed-buffer exposure. See perf-metadata-review.json whole-function witnesses and perf-metadata-check.json modeled accounting control.
